name: Chad
system_note: A military ruler turned elected president in 2024.
snapshot: A Sahel state ruled by Mahamat Déby, who took over when his father was killed in 2021, jailed his main rival and broke a long military alliance with France.
culture: Chad has more than 120 languages, with French and Arabic official and Chadian Arabic the everyday lingua franca. The north is Muslim and largely desert, home to Tubu and Arab nomads; the south is greener, more Christian and agricultural. Lake Chad, once one of Africa's largest lakes, has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s, and its shores support fishing and herding communities across four countries.
society: Oil revenue since 2003 has done little to reduce deep poverty. Chad hosts well over a million refugees, most of them from Sudan's Darfur, in camps along the eastern border. Clashes between herders and farmers are frequent. The army is the backbone of power, built around the Zaghawa clan of the Déby family.
situation: After Idriss Déby was killed fighting rebels in 2021, the army installed his son Mahamat. He won a 2024 election that the opposition called rigged and ended the defence pact with France, whose last troops left in January 2025. Opposition leader and former prime minister Succès Masra was sentenced in 2025 to 20 years in prison. A 2025 constitutional change lengthened presidential terms and removed limits.
power: A presidential republic. A 2025 constitutional change lengthened presidential terms to seven years with no limit; the president appoints the prime minister, and the army, built around the Déby family's Zaghawa clan, is the backbone of power.

conflicts.name: Lake Chad Basin insurgency outside Nigeria (Cameroon Far North, Chad Lac, Niger Diffa)
